ai-at-work.title: On theCUBE Pod: Nvidia steamrolls expectations as Mythos shakes up cybersecurity
ai-at-work.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. might as well be swimming in money like Scrooge McDuck. The artificial intelligence firm had yet another astounding quarter, beating expectations for revenue. With that announcement came
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nvidia crushed earnings expectations again and is throwing money around like a tech drunk uncle, inking major deals with Cisco on AI infrastructure and reportedly dropping nearly $13 billion on Hugging Face. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because AI infrastructure deals and consolidation in the AI tooling space directly shape what platforms, capabilities, and vendor strategies you'll be dealing with in your stacks. Honestly, if you're not already thinking about how AI infrastructure plays are going to reshape your workplace tech decisions, you're going to find yourself explaining vendor pivots to your executives instead of leading them.

ai-at-work.title: Knowledge graphs deliver the real-time context enterprises need to make AI explainable
ai-at-work.excerpt: As AI adoption accelerates and language models become commodities, enterprises are discovering that knowledge graphs provide the critical layer for turning scattered data into usable, real-time contex
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Knowledge graphs are emerging as the connective tissue that turns raw data into actual context that AI systems can understand and explain to humans. This matters because if your AI can't tell you why it made a decision, you've got a liability problem and your users won't trust it. The irony is we spent twenty years trying to organize enterprise data, failed, and now we're paying extra for technology that finally makes that mess intelligible to machines instead of people.

tools-tech.title: 3 surveys deliver the same uncomfortable truth about adopting agentic AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Scaling AI in business is less about technology and more about accountability, governance, and healthy relationships between humans and agents.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Three surveys are telling companies the same thing: they're terrible at actually implementing AI agents, with the real bottleneck being organizational issues rather than the tech itself. For digital workplace leaders, this means your shiny new AI won't matter one bit if your governance structure looks like spaghetti and nobody knows who's responsible when things go wrong. Here's the good news: this is actually fixable, unlike most technology problems, but it requires doing the boring work that nobody wants to do.

digital-culture.title: The craftsmanship revival we kept predicting might finally be real
digital-culture.excerpt: In 2019, I published a book whose English title would be something like From Graft to Craft. I argued that craftsmanship isn’t a sector but a model of work that could in principle apply to any job. Th
digital-culture.dwp_take: A writer's 2019 thesis about "craftsmanship as a work model" rather than just a sector is apparently gaining traction as people reject fragmented, soulless labor. This matters because it signals that organizations claiming to value employee engagement need to actually let people do meaningful work instead of breaking jobs into meaningless tasks. After three decades watching companies say they want craftspeople while designing systems for factory workers, I'll believe the revival is real when I see promotion budgets shift accordingly.

industry-news.title: Top security teams use AI agents, says Hack The Box
industry-news.excerpt: Median solve times are dropping, and more teams are completing the entire challenge board
industry-news.dwp_take: Hack The Box reports that leading security teams are now using AI agents to solve challenges faster, with median solve times dropping and more complete challenge board submissions. This matters because it shows AI is becoming table stakes for security operations, not a future consideration, which means digital workplace leaders need to start thinking about how their security posture changes when their own teams fall behind the AI adoption curve. Honestly, if your security team isn't experimenting with AI agents by now, you're not behind the times, you're already in the past tense.

industry-news.title: Google's Spirit Airlines auction & TrendAI insider threat report
industry-news.excerpt: Google's Spirit Airlines auction & TrendAI insider threat report
industry-news.dwp_take: Google is auctioning off Spirit Airlines' IT assets while TrendAI released new data on insider threats in the workplace. This matters because it shows how quickly digital infrastructure gets liquidated during corporate distress, and insider threat monitoring is becoming table stakes for security teams managing hybrid workforces. Here's the thing though: companies obsess over catching the bad guy stealing data while their own shadow IT and unsanctioned apps create bigger holes than any insider ever could. Fix your fundamentals first.

industry-news.title: 'The threat landscape is moving so quickly': CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz warns AI is raising the stakes in cybersecurity – and the firm is poised to capitalize on ‘the largest market opportunity in our history’
industry-news.excerpt: With concerns over AI security rising, Kurtz believes CrowdStrike can position itself as the go-to provider for enterprises
industry-news.dwp_take: CrowdStrike's CEO is warning that AI is accelerating cyber threats while positioning his company as the solution to defend against them. For digital workplace leaders, this means security concerns are becoming table stakes in every infrastructure decision you make, especially as AI tools proliferate across your organization. Here's the thing: every security vendor in history has declared their current moment "the largest market opportunity ever," so take the sky-is-falling rhetoric with a grain of salt while still taking your actual security posture seriously.

industry-news.title: Basware to acquire Trustpair to strengthen payment fraud prevention
industry-news.excerpt: The deal will combine Basware’s invoice lifecycle management platform with Trustpair’s technology for validating supplier accounts and preventing fraudulent payments
industry-news.dwp_take: Basware is buying Trustpair to merge invoice management with supplier verification technology, creating a more complete fraud prevention package. Digital workplace pros need to pay attention because payment fraud keeps getting more sophisticated, and integrated solutions that catch problems upstream during the invoice stage actually matter operationally. Here's the thing though: every vendor acquisition announcement claims to create this magical unified platform, but the real test is whether their actual customers see genuine workflow improvements or just a clunkier tool that does two mediocre jobs instead of one good one.
